intro: Verb phrases that add a shade of meaning: a sudden start, a slow process, an ending, a result.
p.voy entendiendo.consejo: «Ir» + gerund marks a slow process: «voy mejorando», «va oscureciendo».
p.llevo leídos.consejo: «Llevar» + participle counts what is done so far and agrees: «llevo leídas diez páginas».
p.acaba perdonándolo.consejo: «Acabar» + gerund is to end up doing something. It is not «acabar de», which means «a moment ago».
p.llegó a escribir.glosa: he/she went so far as to write
p.llegó a escribir.consejo: «Llegar a» + infinitive marks an extreme point: «llegó a gritar». The ll sounds y.
p.me puse a leer.consejo: «Ponerse a» + infinitive is to start suddenly: «se puso a llover».
p.se echa a llorar.consejo: «Echarse a» is used with reír, llorar and correr: «se echó a reír». It is an abrupt start.
p.tengo hecha.consejo: «Tener» + participle gives the result: «tengo hecha la cena». The participle agrees with the thing done.
p.vengo diciendo.glosa: I have been saying (for some time)
p.vengo diciendo.consejo: «Venir» + gerund: an action that lasts up to now. «Vengo diciéndolo desde hace años».
p.anda buscando.glosa: he/she is going around looking for
p.anda buscando.consejo: «Andar» + gerund: a repeated action with no fixed course: «anda buscando trabajo».
p.poco a poco.consejo: It is a set phrase that never changes. It goes very well with «ir» + gerund.
p.capítulo.consejo: It has an accent on the i: ka-PI-tu-lo. A novel is divided into chapters.
p.final.consejo: The stress is at the end: fi-NAL. «Al final» means «in the end».
b1.texto:
- a sudden start: **ponerse a** + infinitive; **echarse a** reír, llorar, correr; **romper a** llorar
- little by little: **ir** + gerund. **Voy entendiendo.**
- for some time now: **llevar** + gerund (llevo dos horas esperando); **venir** + gerund (vengo diciéndolo desde hace años)
- here and there, without focus: **andar** + gerund. **Anda diciendo** que se va.
- ending up: **acabar** + gerund. **Acabó aceptando.**
- going as far as: **llegar a** + infinitive. **Llegó a** insultarme.

With a **participle**, which agrees with the object, the phrase shows a result:

- **llevar**: **llevo leídas** cien páginas (so far)
- **tener**: **tengo hecha** la cena (done and ready)
- **dejar**: lo **dejó dicho** (he left word)
b2.f1.texto: I have read ten chapters so far.
b2.f2.texto: At first I understood nothing, but I'm gradually getting it.
b2.f3.texto: I started reading it and gave up.
b2.f4.texto: In the end the main character bursts into tears and ends up forgiving him.
b2.f6.texto: Relax. The author went so far as to write three different endings.
b2.f7.texto: My sister has been looking around for that book for a month.
b4.titulo: Each phrase, a shade of meaning
b4.texto:
- ponerse a + infinitive: a sudden start (se puso a llover)
- echarse a + infinitive: bursting out (se echó a reír)
- ir + gerund: little by little (voy mejorando)
- venir + gerund: for some time now (vengo notando cambios)
- acabar + gerund: ending up (acabé cediendo)
- llegar a + infinitive: going as far as (llegó a gritar)
- llevar / tener + participle: the result so far (llevo escritas diez páginas)
b4.e1.texto: I have been telling the truth for years.
b5.f0.texto: The lamp draws a yellow circle over the open pages.
b5.f1.texto: Rosa reads slowly, her finger following each line.
b5.f2.texto: At first the words weigh like stones, but little by little they turn light.
b5.f3.texto: Rosa has already read ten chapters.
b5.f4.texto: The whole night smells of tea and old wood.
b5.f5.texto: Suddenly, the main character bursts into tears in the rain of the book.
b5.f6.texto: Rosa starts reading faster, her heart restless.
b5.f7.texto: Outside, the wind taps the windowpanes with cold fingers.
b5.f8.texto: In the end, the man in the book ends up forgiving his brother.
b5.f9.texto: Rosa closes the book, switches off the lamp and smiles in the dark.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «echarse a reír» is to burst out laughing.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Llegar a» marks an extreme; you do not say «llegarse a reír».
b6.pregunta: Choose the verb of a sudden start.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «ir» + gerund is a gradual process.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That would be «voy a entender» or «entenderé».
b8.frase: Al principio no entendía nada pero voy entendiendo
b8.traduccion: At first I understood nothing, but I'm gradually getting it
b9.o0.refuerzo: That is it: «acabar» + gerund is to end up doing something.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Acabar de» means «a moment ago», a different sense.
b9.o2.refuerzo: The participle does not form this phrase with «acabar».
b9.pregunta: You ended up accepting: choose the form.
b11.o0.refuerzo: That would express purpose. «Llegar a» + infinitive marks an extreme.
b11.o1: llegó hasta el extremo de insultarme
b11.o1.refuerzo: Well done: insulting was an extreme point he reached.
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: it agrees with «páginas», feminine plural.
b12.o1.refuerzo: It is masculine singular and does not agree with «páginas».
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Llevo escribiendo» needs a length of time: «llevo dos horas escribiendo».
p.capítulos.consejo: Plural of «capítulo», chapter. The accent is on the i: ka-PI-tu-los.
p.entendía.consejo: Imperfect of «entender», to understand. The accent separates the vowels: en-ten-DI-a.
p.cuentes.consejo: Subjunctive of «contar», to tell. The ue is a diphthong: KWEN-tes.
p.finales.consejo: Plural of «final», end. Stress on NA: fi-NA-les.
p.mejorando.consejo: Gerund of «mejorar», to improve. Stress on RAN: me-ho-RAN-do.
p.páginas.consejo: Plural of «página», page. The g before i is h, and the stress is on PA.
p.siguiendo.consejo: Gerund of «seguir», to follow. The u of «gu» is silent: si-GIEN-do.
p.pesan.consejo: From «pesar», to weigh. Stress on PE: PE-san.
p.ligeras.consejo: Feminine plural of «ligero», light. The g before e is h.
p.leídos.consejo: Plural participle of «leer», to read. The accent breaks the diphthong: le-I-dos.
p.deprisa.consejo: It means quickly. The stress falls on PRI: de-PRI-sa.
p.inquieto.consejo: The qu is k, and the ie is a diphthong: in-KIE-to.
p.perdonando.consejo: Gerund of «perdonar», to forgive. Stress on NAN: per-do-NAN-do.
p.oscuridad.consejo: Ends in -dad, so it is feminine: «la oscuridad». Stress on DAD.
p.reír.consejo: The tilde on the í separates the vowels: rre-IR, the stress on the last syllable.
p.echó.consejo: Past tense of «echar», to throw. Stress on CHO: e-CHO.
p.acabé.consejo: Past tense of «acabar», to finish. The accent marks the stress on BE.
p.aceptando.consejo: Gerund of «aceptar», to accept. The c before e is th in Spain.
p.extremo.consejo: Masculine, «el extremo». The x sounds ks. Stress on TRE.
p.insultarme.consejo: «Me» at the end means «me». The stress is on TAR.
p.escritas.consejo: Feminine plural participle of «escribir», to write. Stress on KRI.
